newsitem.title: USA: State Street holders approve shr increase.
newsitem.headline: State Street holders approve shr increase.

text.p: State Street Corp said shareholders at the annual meeting Wednesday approved an increase in authorized shares in order to make possible a two-for-one stock split in May, State Street said.
The shareholders also approved changing the name of the company from the former State Street Boston Corp.

Chairman and chief executive Marshall Carter also restated State Street's opposition to a request by Bank of New York Co Inc seeking approval to raise its stake in State Street to 9.99 percent from 4.9 percent.

According to a press release, Carter told the meeting that State Streeet believes the Massachusetts Board of Bank Incorporation acted correctly in turning down the Bank of New York request to raise its stake. He said, "We also expect that our arguments will prevail at the federal level."

He said should the Bank of New York effort or any other transaction evolve into an "unwelcome" takeover attempt "the support of our board and our stockholders will ensure State Street's ability to respond in a manner appropriate to the interest of our stockholders."
Bank of New York is suing to get the Massachusetts ruling overturned.
